T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive it as a fashion or lifestyle accessory, because they are willing to pay a premium for stylish, comfortable earplugs that complement their personal style. Who benefits: Consumers seeking stylish, comfortable hearing protection; Hellberg Safety benefits by capturing premium pricing and brand differentiation.. Why behaviour changes: If consumers view hearing protection as a fashion item, they will be motivated to own multiple pairs or styles, increasing purchase frequency and willingness to pay above the standard price point.. How value is captured: Hellberg can charge a premium price for design-led products, sell through fashion retailers, and build a lifestyle brand that differentiates it from generic industrial earplugs.. Assumptions: Consumers currently perceive hearing protection as utilitarian rather than fashion.; A design-led proposition can be produced at scale without compromising safety standards.; Fashion retailers are willing to stock and promote a differentiated consumer line.. Predictions: In a test offering a stylish, design-led earplug at a premium price, purchase intent among fashion-conscious consumers will be at least 20% higher than for a standard, functional earplug.; Surveyed consumers will rank style and comfort as top factors in choosing hearing protection, above price or safety requirements..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive it as a safety requirement for specific high-risk activities (e.g., construction, rock concerts, or industrial work), because they will purchase it as a necessary protective item. Who benefits: Safety-conscious consumers in high-risk environments; Hellberg Safety benefits by selling purpose-specific, certified products and potentially securing contracts with employers.. Why behaviour changes: If hearing protection is framed as a mandatory safety item for a particular use case, consumers will act on the requirement rather than personal style or fashion, leading to higher purchase frequency.. How value is captured: Hellberg can price and market products as safety essentials, sell through industrial and safety retailers, and build a reputation for compliance and reliability in high-risk sectors.. Assumptions: There is a measurable demand for hearing protection in specific high-risk activities.; Safety regulations or employer requirements will continue to drive purchase decisions in these segments.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for certified, purpose-specific protection.. Predictions: In a test offering a purpose-specific earplug marketed as a safety requirement, purchase intent among workers and concert-goers will be at least 30% higher than for a generic, unbranded earplug.; Surveyed consumers will cite safety compliance or employer requirements as the primary reason for purchasing hearing protection..

Test "Fashion vs Safety Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging and purchase intent measurement.. Sample: 500 adults (age 18-45) recruited via an online panel, split equally between two groups: Fashion Group (n=250) and Safety Group (n=250).. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (WTP) for a styled vs safety-specific earplug.. Predictions: T1: Fashion Group will show purchase intent at least 20% higher than Safety Group, and WTP will be higher for the styled earplug.; T2: Safety Group will show purchase intent at least 20% higher than Fashion Group, and WTP will be higher for the safety-specific earplug.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the two groups is at least 20 percentage points and the Safety Group's purchase intent is at least 20% higher than the Fashion Group, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is less than 20 points and the Fashion Group's purchase intent is at least 20% higher, conclude T1 is supported. If neither condition is met, the test is inconclusive and no expansion is recommended.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Uncertainty: The evidence base is limited to company assertions and a simulated wear test; no real consumer data shows willingness to pay for fashion-led hearing protection or that safety requirements drive purchase decisions.. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

Test "Consumer Proposition Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging and choice-based conjoint design.. Sample: 500 adults recruited via an online panel, stratified by age and gender to reflect the target consumer base.. Measure: 1) Purchase intent: 7-point Likert scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely). 2) Willingness to pay: 7-point Likert scale (1 = very low, 7 = very high). 3) Messaging preference: 3-point scale (lifestyle vs functional vs specific-use).. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay for a lifestyle-branded proposition than for a functional proposition.; T2: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay for a specific-use proposition than for a lifestyle proposition.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for the lifestyle proposition exceeds the functional proposition by at least 1.5 points on the 7-point scale, and the difference is statistically significant (p<0.05), then T1 is favoured. If the average purchase intent for the specific-use proposition exceeds the lifestyle proposition by at least 1.5 points, and the difference is statistically significant, then T2 is favoured. If neither difference reaches the threshold, the test is inconclusive and no expansion is recommended.. Cost: 2000 euros, 6 weeks.

After viewing both descriptions, participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and willingness to pay (EUR).. Sample: 400 participants (200 outdoor/recreational enthusiasts and 200 safety professionals/employers) from Europe, recruited via an online panel.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and willingness to pay (EUR) for each messaging condition.. Predictions: T1: Outdoor/recreational segment will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay for the lifestyle message than for the compliance message.; T2: Safety professionals/employers will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay for the compliance message than for the lifestyle message.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for the lifestyle message in the outdoor segment is at least 5 points higher than for the compliance message, proceed with a differentiated lifestyle proposition. If the average purchase intent for the compliance message in the safety segment is at least 5 points higher than for the lifestyle message, proceed with a differentiated compliance proposition.
